title: React Native and Vega OS integration
lead: These two directories provide source code for integration into external native projects. Passing the repository’s type checks and unit tests does not establish that the resulting apps build or play on a device.

blocks.text: React Native and Expo

apps/react-native provides App.tsx, the source list, DVR logic, and state management. Its declared dependencies are Expo ~54.0.0, React Native 0.81.5, React 19.1.0, and bitmovin-player-react-native 1.28.0 pinned exactly. It is not a complete Expo app; integrate it into a compatible external project.

The wrapper's native Player defaults are 3.126.0 through Swift Package Manager on iOS/tvOS and 3.165.0+jason on Android. Keep this wrapper-supported combination; the standalone native samples have separate SDK pins.

blocks.title: External project creation example from the README
blocks.text:
npx create-expo-app@latest dvr-showcase
cd dvr-showcase
npx expo install bitmovin-player-react-native@1.28.0 expo-crypto react-native-url-polyfill@4.0.0

The dependencies generated by @latest change over time. Compare the generated project with the versions in apps/react-native/package.json. The native Player module requires a development build; Expo Go cannot run it.
Register the Player config plugin in the external project's app.json or equivalent app.config. Merge the following entry while preserving existing plugins.

blocks.title: Player plugin entry in app.json

items: Run sync-env.sh and build and synchronize the shared UI as described in the common preparation.

Copy App.tsx, src/, and the generated .env from apps/react-native into the external Expo project. The Player license is read from EXPO_PUBLIC_BITMOVIN_PLAYER_LICENSE_KEY, and the optional Analytics license from EXPO_PUBLIC_BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY.

Render the copied App.tsx component from the external project’s entry point. In an Expo Router project, connect it to the route screen that should display the player; copying the file alone does not replace that screen.
Allow the external app’s bundle identifier or application ID on your Player license and, if used, Analytics license. There is no fixed public application ID for this integration.

For a custom UI, bundle the JavaScript and CSS from assets/webui/ into the external app’s iOS/Android projects, and update WEBUI_JS and WEBUI_CSS in App.tsx to point to the actual files. The current addresses are integration placeholders.
Run an iOS or Android development build from the external Expo project.

blocks.text: Version 1.27 moved iOS Player and Google IMA dependencies from CocoaPods to Swift Package Manager. When upgrading an existing app, remove explicit Player, Player Core, Analytics, and IMA pod dependencies; keep the bridge, Expo, and optional Cast pods. With the plugin registered, rerun iOS prebuild below. Install pods if needed and open the generated .xcworkspace. For integration without prebuild, follow the official migration guide listed in Sources. The installed package's ios/dependencies.json defines exact Player and IMA versions. Rebuild and check framework embedding and Release archives after integration.

blocks.title: Refresh native iOS configuration after installing or upgrading
blocks.text: npx expo prebuild --platform ios

blocks.title: Choose the target command in the external Expo project
blocks.text:
npx expo run:ios
npx expo run:android

The screen includes Default, Sports, Live (DVR), and Cinema UI choices; source buttons; Live edge; −10/−30/−60-second controls; Allow DVR; state; an event log; and Show configuration. iOS starts with HLS and offers HLS/progressive MP4; DASH types and presets are hidden there. Android also offers DASH.

Show configuration edits the required HTTP/HTTPS source URL, type, optional title/poster URL, start offset in seconds, and its Start/End/SDK default reference. Signed offsets are allowed: Start refers to the beginning of the media/DVR window, End to the end/live edge. The SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Blank title/poster/offset fields remove those optional values.

URL validation uses the locally imported URL from react-native-url-polyfill 4.0.0. Older native global URL implementations leave protocol and hostname unimplemented, which would reject valid sources before loading. The local parser leaves global URL and the SDK media shims unchanged.

Autoplay and Mute on startup apply at player creation. Start offsets and buffer durations accept finite decimal seconds. Blank buffer keeps the SDK default (iOS 0, Android 50); iOS 0 lets the SDK choose a duration. This form requires a positive Android buffer target because zero is not its automatic setting. Maximum bitrate accepts whole bits per second: 1–2,147,483,647 on Android and 1–9,007,199,254,740,991 on iOS; blank means no cap. The native bridge converts bitrate to an integer, Android uses a signed 32-bit value, and JavaScript cannot represent integers above its safe limit exactly. Fractions and out-of-range values are rejected before recreation.

Apply and recreate player validates the whole draft, recreates the player, and reloads the selected source from its start offset. Playback position resets and playback starts according to Autoplay. The complete source, chosen UI, log, and Allow DVR setting are retained. Invalid or unchanged settings do not recreate the player. Reset draft only discards edits; it does not change playback. Preset source buttons still load immediately. Allow DVR remains an application helper rather than an editable SDK playback property.

blocks.title: Check logic and types from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm --filter @showcase/react-native test
pnpm --filter @showcase/react-native typecheck

Type checking covers App.tsx, the configuration panel, the source list, and pure logic. App interaction tests use mocked native/player objects to check edits, validation, Apply/Reset, source retention, and recreation. They do not verify external Expo project generation, native builds, native/WebView layout, or playback. A compatible external Expo project and device/simulator build are still required.
Vega OS and Kepler

Vega OS is a separate runtime from Android-based Fire TV. apps/vega connects the modular Web Player to a W3C media element and uses React Native/Kepler screen components. It does not use bitmovin-player-ui, which requires a browser document. Dependencies include Player 8.138.0-beta.28, React Native 0.72.0, React 18.2.0, and Amazon device packages. As of 2026-10-20, the official Vega sample supports only the 8.138.0-beta.XX channel; beta.28 is its latest listed release and remains pinned here. General Web releases are not declared supported by that sample.

items: Prepare the Amazon Vega/Kepler development tools and a compatible Fire TV device or Vega simulator. Check each provider’s terms for the CLI, SDK, and device packages.
Integrate the sources into a configured Kepler project. This repository alone does not provide a standalone device build.
Replace src/polyfills.ts with the compatibility layer required by the runtime. Base64, DOMParser, W3C media, and WebCrypto are needed; the minimal template alone cannot provide playback.

Set your licenses in globals in the entry point before registering the app. App.tsx itself does not read .env. The Player’s tweaks.app_id example is com.showcase.dvr.vega; align it with your own configuration and license permissions.
Build, install, and launch from the Kepler project. Check video output, seeking, return to live, recovery after a position expires, and remote controls on the device.

blocks.title: Kepler entry-point configuration example
blocks.text:
globalThis.BITMOVIN_PLAYER_LICENSE_KEY = "<YOUR_PLAYER_LICENSE_KEY>";
globalThis.BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY = "";

blocks.title: Run from a configured Kepler project
blocks.text:
react-native build-kepler --build-type Debug
kepler device install-app --dir .
kepler device launch-app

The screen includes source selection, Live edge, −10/−30/−60-second controls, Allow DVR, state, logs, and Show configuration. Autoplay and mute are initially enabled. It does not provide dedicated play/pause buttons, audio/subtitle/quality selection, or TV remote key-event handling. DRM modules are also excluded.

Show configuration edits an HTTP/HTTPS source URL, HLS/DASH/progressive MP4 type, optional title/poster URL, signed start offset in seconds and Start/End/SDK default reference. Start means beginning of media/DVR window, End means end/live edge; the SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Blank title/poster/offset fields remove those optional values. The Kepler screen has no artwork overlay, so a poster value is stored with the source without adding a visible poster.

URL validation uses a local URL import from react-native-url-polyfill 4.0.0 because React Native 0.72 leaves the global protocol and hostname getters unimplemented. The local parser leaves global URL and the Vega SDK media shims unchanged. Include the dependency from apps/vega/package.json in the external Kepler project.

Autoplay and Mute on startup apply at player creation. Separate audio/video forward buffer targets are in seconds; this form accepts positive values, and blank keeps the SDK default of 40 seconds per media type. Live windows can limit the effective buffer. Maximum video bitrate is a positive adaptation cap in bits per second; blank means no cap. Numbers must be finite decimals. Format, buffering and adaptation support still depends on the stream, engine and target device.

Apply and recreate player validates the draft, waits for the previous player to close, and reloads the selected source from its start offset. Playback position resets and playback starts according to Autoplay; the selected/custom source, log and Allow DVR setting are retained. Invalid or unchanged settings do not recreate the player. Reset draft only discards edits. Preset source buttons still load immediately. The HTML Player UI remains disabled on Vega; Allow DVR controls an application helper.

blocks.title: Check the screen and logic from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega test
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega typecheck

Vega type checking includes the actual App, settings/control panels and video-surface JSX against installed SDK, React Native and Kepler declarations. App/session tests use mocked native/media/player objects to check edits, validation, Apply/Reset, retained settings and changes during initialization/cleanup. They do not verify native layout, TV focus or keyboard input, Kepler builds, or playback. Build and test these controls in a configured Kepler project on the target device.
